purpose: Defines the zero-copy streaming ingestion engine, auto-fingerprinting detector, and orchestrator adapters for parsing Claude Code, Antigravity (AGY), Codex, and OpenCode session logs into CanonicalTranscript representations.
scope: Covers crates/lumen-session: SessionAdapter trait, AdapterCapabilities, fingerprint detection, ClaudeCodeAdapter, AgyAdapter, CodexAdapter, OpenCodeAdapter, PreCompact snapshot merge, and IngestionError.

api_surface.name: SessionAdapter
api_surface.signature: pub trait SessionAdapter: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> &'static str; fn matches_fingerprint(&self, sample: &str) -> bool; fn capabilities(&self) -> AdapterCapabilities; fn parse_stream<'a>(&self, reader: Box<dyn BufRead + 'a>) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, IngestionError>; }
api_surface.description: Streaming parser trait implemented by orchestrator adapters to project newline-delimited logs into CanonicalTranscript.
error_conditions: IngestionError::MalformedJson is reserved for a whole-input failure (e.g. the reader yields non-UTF8 bytes before any line boundary is found, or the sample is empty when a non-empty stream was expected) -- a single malformed LINE within an otherwise-readable stream is never this error; it is skipped and recorded per CRIT-LUMEN-025 instead, and parse_stream continues.
IngestionError::UnrecognizedFormat if log sample does not match known orchestrators

api_surface.name: AdapterCapabilities
api_surface.signature: pub struct AdapterCapabilities { pub has_token_usage: bool, pub has_tool_results: bool, pub has_shell_commands: bool, pub has_file_events: bool, pub has_lifecycle_hooks: bool, pub supports_incremental_offsets: bool, pub supports_cost_estimation: bool }
api_surface.description: Observability declaration exposing what telemetric capabilities are supported by the target orchestrator.

api_surface.name: detect_orchestrator
api_surface.description: Sub-millisecond fingerprint detector inspecting the first 2048 bytes of a session log to identify Claude Code, AGY, Codex, or OpenCode.
error_conditions: Returns None if byte sample contains insufficient or ambiguous headers

api_surface.name: merge_precompact_snapshots
api_surface.description: Applies the max() cumulative token merge invariant across pre-compaction snapshots to prevent double-counting on compacted sessions.

api_surface.name: synthetic_50mb_session
api_surface.signature: pub fn synthetic_50mb_session(orchestrator: OrchestratorKind, seed: u64) -> impl BufRead
api_surface.description: Deterministic (seeded) fixture generator in crates/lumen-fixtures that programmatically expands a real corpus template (e.g. real_claude_session_dump()) to at least 50MB, in-memory, for CRIT-LUMEN-029 benchmarking without requiring a checked-in binary fixture. Return type intentionally deviates from the other corpus/*.rs fixtures (which return &'static str literals): this fixture is generated/owned data, not a static string, since a 50MB literal is impractical to check in.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a session file's first 2048 bytes contain the JSON keys "sessionId" and "parentUuid" together (real, confirmed top-level fields present on Claude Code JSONL entries -- verified this session against this conversation's own real transcript and the lumen-fixtures corpus), THE SYSTEM SHALL identify the orchestrator as OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode in under 1 millisecond.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): this was the one detection criterion never tightened to literal bytes while every sibling (021/106/107/166) was. Tightened using fields already confirmed real and used elsewhere this session (lumen-fixtures's real_claude_session_dump fixture carries sessionId/parentUuid per line). Whether these two keys specifically appear within the file's FIRST line/2048 bytes (as opposed to being real fields present somewhere in the file generally) has not been re-verified with a fresh byte-offset check -- flagged as a residual, narrower open item rather than left as vague prose.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a session file's first 2048 bytes contain the JSON key "step_index" alongside a "source" value of "USER_EXPLICIT" or "MODEL", THE SYSTEM SHALL identify the orchestrator as OrchestratorKind::Antigravity in under 1 millisecond.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The field names step_index/source were already correct, but the exact value vocabulary (USER_EXPLICIT|MODEL, not e.g. user|assistant) had never been checked against a real file until this session -- verified directly by reading a live ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl on 2026-08-20. Tightened from a vague "AGY headers" description to the exact bytes now confirmed real.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN ClaudeCodeAdapter parses an assistant message containing tool_use blocks, THE SYSTEM SHALL extract tool_name, call_id, and typed ToolIntent in the CanonicalTurn.

WHEN ClaudeCodeAdapter parses message.usage, THE SYSTEM SHALL extract input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, and cache_read_input_tokens; a missing (absent) usage or missing individual field defaults to 0 via ordinary Option handling. Note: input_tokens/output_tokens are NOT among the fields CRIT-LUMEN-163 requires explicit-JSON-null rejection for -- ccusage's real corruption-check list (the source of CRIT-LUMEN-163) does not include them, so no real evidence exists that Claude Code ever emits them as explicit null; if that changes, CRIT-LUMEN-163's field list should be extended, not this criterion.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): CRIT-LUMEN-163's explicit-null-rejection list omits input_tokens/output_tokens, which this criterion requires extracting -- left genuinely undefined for a null value on those two fields. Clarified rather than silently expanding CRIT-163's field list without real evidence those two fields are ever null in practice.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN merging pre-compaction snapshots, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute input_tokens = max(final_input, max(snapshot_inputs)) and cache_read_tokens = max(final_cache_read, max(snapshot_cache_reads)); IF snapshots is empty, THE SYSTEM SHALL return final_transcript unchanged (an empty max-set contributes nothing, not zero).

IF a JSONL log contains corrupted, truncated, or non-UTF8 lines, THE SYSTEM SHALL skip the malformed line, record a parse-failure entry (session_id, line number, raw byte offset, and the parse error) that SURVIVES the parse_stream call -- returned alongside or attached to the CanonicalTranscript, so a caller can inspect it, not merely logged to stderr and discarded -- and continue parsing without panicking. Durable cross-process persistence of that record (e.g. to a SQLite store) is out of scope for lumen-session itself; see non_goals.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior wording ("record a warning") was verified this session to describe behavior no adapter actually implements -- claude.rs:60-66 silently `continue`s with no warning recorded at all, and ccusage's real adapters (common/jsonl.rs) do the same industry-wide. Audit finding (2026-08-20): "durable, queryable" overclaimed relative to what this criterion's own reasoning permitted (an in-memory Vec) and relative to non_goals' delegation to a crate ("session-daemon") that doesn't exist in this workspace -- the real crates are lumen-store (SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE) and lumen-daemon (SPEC-LUMEN-004-DAEMON), now named correctly in non_goals below. Reworded to require only what lumen-session itself can own: a record that survives the call, not a claim about cross-process durability this crate doesn't control.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN ClaudeCodeAdapter encounters a real top-level isSidechain: bool field on a JSONL entry (confirmed via direct grep against 31 real local ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl transcripts, 2026-08-21: 22 of 31 files contain the camelCase isSidechain spelling, zero contain a snake_case is_sidechain spelling), THE SYSTEM SHALL treat entries with isSidechain=true as belonging to a subagent/parallel-conversation branch distinct from the main chain, excluding them from the main transcript's turns entirely; WHEN a sibling subagents/<worker>.jsonl file exists alongside a session's main transcript file, THE SYSTEM SHALL unconditionally parse it as a child CanonicalTranscript linked via parent_session_id to the parent session AND set that child transcript's subagent_role to the real <worker> path segment (see SPEC-LUMEN-001-MODEL's CanonicalTranscript.subagent_role), so SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS's AttributionAccumulator recursion (CRIT-LUMEN-149) has a concrete role to key on. This linkage is unconditional and requires no back-reference check: a subagents/<worker>.jsonl file is linked whether or not any isSidechain=true entry in the main file specifically references it, and an isSidechain=true entry with no corresponding subagents/<worker>.jsonl file is simply excluded from the main transcript without error -- in neither case does the absence of a matching counterpart on the other side cause a parse failure.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior wording (*.meta.json files carrying tool_use_id/spawnDepth) was never verified against real data and does not match what was actually confirmed this session: ccusage's real, cross-validated Claude adapter keys subagent detection on a real top-level isSidechain boolean field PLUS separate sibling subagents/<worker>.jsonl transcript files -- not a *.meta.json sidecar. Linkage now targets CanonicalTranscript.parent_session_id, which already exists in the IR (crates/lumen-model/src/transcript.rs:14), rather than a tool_use_id/spawnDepth pair that was never confirmed to exist in real data. Audit finding (2026-08-20) added the orphaned-entry/orphaned-file non-error clause, previously unspecified. Correction (2026-08-21): the field name was originally written as snake_case is_sidechain, which does not match any real Claude Code transcript on this machine; direct grep against 31 real files confirmed the true field is camelCase isSidechain, and the implementation (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs) was fixed to match. The orphan-linking clause was also self-contradictory in its original wording (its first sentence mandated linking any sibling subagents/<worker>.jsonl file unconditionally, while its last sentence mandated leaving an unreferenced one unlinked) -- corrected to state the actual, tested behavior: linkage is unconditional and never requires a back-reference.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN AgyAdapter parses a step whose type is "PLANNER_RESPONSE", THE SYSTEM SHALL extract that step's thinking field into CanonicalTurn.text when present, and SHALL extract each entry of that step's tool_calls array (name plus args, where each arg value is itself a JSON-encoded string requiring a second parse pass -- e.g. "DirectoryPath":"\"/Users/gabe/...\"") into CanonicalToolCall entries. IF the second (inner) JSON parse pass on an arg value fails, THE SYSTEM SHALL retain that arg's raw, unparsed string value rather than dropping the argument or failing the whole tool_call/entry.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Confirmed correct in shape by direct read of a real transcript.jsonl this session (2026-08-20) -- PLANNER_RESPONSE entries do carry step_index/source/type/status/created_at plus thinking and tool_calls[]. Extended from thinking-only to also require tool_calls extraction (previously undocumented) and to flag the double-JSON-encoding of tool_call args as a real, confirmed parsing gotcha, not a hypothetical one. Audit finding (2026-08-20) added the inner-parse-failure fallback, previously unspecified.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF an empty session file is supplied, THE SYSTEM SHALL return a valid CanonicalTranscript with 0 turns and 0 token usage without erroring.

WHEN memory-mapped file parsing is requested on a 50MB session file, THE SYSTEM SHALL parse all turns in under 35 milliseconds, as measured by the CRIT-LUMEN-116 criterion benchmark (crates/lumen-session/benches/) running on whatever hardware executes it -- this is a relative regression-guard bound tracked against that benchmark's own recorded baseline over time, not an absolute cross-machine hardware guarantee (no specific CI/dev hardware spec is asserted).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): the bound had no stated hardware/CI baseline, making it non-reproducible across machines as literally worded. Scoped honestly as a relative regression guard tied to CRIT-LUMEN-116's own benchmark rather than fabricating a specific hardware spec that was never actually pinned down.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a session file's first 2048 bytes contain the JSON substring "event_msg" or "response_item" alongside a top-level "type" key, and no ClaudeCode or Antigravity fingerprint markers matched first, THE SYSTEM SHALL identify the orchestrator as OrchestratorKind::Codex via detect_orchestrator.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior wording (choices/prompt_tokens/thread_id) fingerprinted a raw OpenAI Chat Completions API shape confirmed this session, via a real local ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl file, to not exist in real Codex CLI output -- real rollout lines use the envelope {timestamp, ordinal, type, payload} with type values event_msg/response_item/custom_tool_call/function_call, cross-validated independently by ccusage's real Rust Codex adapter (byte-matches literally on "type":"event_msg"/"type":"token_count").

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a session file's first 2048 bytes begin with the 16-byte SQLite file magic header "SQLite format 3\0", and no ClaudeCode, Antigravity, or Codex fingerprint markers matched first, THE SYSTEM SHALL identify the orchestrator as OrchestratorKind::OpenCode via detect_orchestrator against the current, SQLite-backed OpenCode generation (session/message/part/event tables).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior wording ("action":"run"/"observation":) fingerprinted an action/observation/source JSONL shape confirmed this session, via CodeBurn's own source comment plus direct inspection of a real local ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db, to have zero basis in any real OpenCode version, ever. Current OpenCode is SQLite-backed, not JSONL, so byte-content fingerprinting must key on the SQLite file magic rather than a JSON substring.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN CodexAdapter::matches_fingerprint or OpenCodeAdapter::matches_fingerprint is invoked on any sample, THE SYSTEM SHALL return exactly the boolean that detect_orchestrator(sample) == Some(OrchestratorKind::Codex) (respectively Some(OrchestratorKind::OpenCode)) would return, so the two independently-coded detection paths cannot drift apart.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior known-drift gap (spaced vs. unspaced action:run) is moot now that CRIT-LUMEN-107's ground truth is the SQLite magic header rather than an action/observation substring -- this criterion is restated as the general drift-prevention rule without a carried-forward bug.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN CodexAdapter::parse_stream reads a line whose "type" is "event_msg" and whose payload.type is "item_completed", THE SYSTEM SHALL append one CanonicalTurn with turn.role set to TurnRole::User when payload.item.type == "UserMessage", TurnRole::Assistant when payload.item.type == "AgentMessage", or TurnRole::ToolResult when payload.item.type == "CommandExecution" or "Reasoning"; FOR any other payload.item.type value, THE SYSTEM SHALL append the turn with TurnRole::System rather than dropping it or erroring, since a future/uncatalogued item type is a real possibility, not a malformed-line case. THE SYSTEM SHALL set turn.text from the item's text content when present, and SHALL set CanonicalTranscript.session_id from the thread_id carried on this same item_completed payload (thread_id does not appear at the envelope's top level in real Codex output). Replaces the prior stub, which always returned session_id="codex-session" with zero turns regardless of input, and the prior criterion's wrong assumption that turns derive from a choices[] array.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Rewritten against the real Codex CLI rollout format, verified this session both against a live local ~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl file and cross-validated via ccusage's real Rust Codex adapter (which reaches the same event_msg/item_completed structure). Codex also emits a second, distinct custom_tool_call/custom_tool_call_output (and separately function_call/function_call_output) pair for tool invocations, not covered by this criterion -- tracked as a follow-up, not fabricated here without a directly-observed example of that specific pair's full shape. Audit finding (2026-08-20) added the explicit TurnRole::System default for uncatalogued item types, previously silently unspecified.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN CodexAdapter::parse_stream reads a line whose "type" is "event_msg" and whose payload.type is "token_count" AND that payload carries a total_token_usage object, THE SYSTEM SHALL read it (not a per-line delta) and set TokenEconomics.input_tokens/output_tokens to the LATEST such reading observed (last-write, not summed -- Codex's token_count events are already cumulative running totals, unlike OpenCodeAdapter's per-line deltas), keeping reasoning_output_tokens (when present on the payload) as a value distinct from output_tokens rather than folded into it. IF a token_count payload lacks total_token_usage, THE SYSTEM SHALL leave input_tokens/output_tokens at their last-known value (no update, not a reset to zero). Replaces the prior stub's unconditional TokenEconomics::calculate(0, 0, 0, 0, ...) and the prior criterion's wrong assumption of an OpenAI-style prompt_tokens/completion_tokens shape summed across lines.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Rewritten against the real Codex CLI format (event_msg/token_count carrying a cumulative total_token_usage/last_token_usage pair, verified directly against a live local rollout file). The cumulative-not-summed distinction matters: naively summing per-line token_count values as if they were deltas (the OpenCodeAdapter pattern) would massively over-count, since Codex already reports running totals. reasoning_output_tokens as a distinct field is a new finding from ccusage's real Codex adapter, not previously represented anywhere in Lumen's model. Audit finding (2026-08-20) added the missing-total_token_usage fallback, previously unspecified.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN CodexAdapter::parse_stream reads a line whose "type" is "event_msg" and whose payload.type is "thread_settings_applied", THE SYSTEM SHALL record payload.thread_settings.service_tier (e.g. "Standard", "Fast") on the transcript's economics/attribution data so downstream pricing lookups can select the correct cost tier for that session's remaining turns.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: New finding from ccusage's real Codex adapter (rust/adapters/codex/src/parser.rs): a real, per-session cost-tier concept Lumen's model has no equivalent of today. Exact field placement (which struct carries service_tier) is left to implementation; the criterion establishes that this signal must be captured, not dropped.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN OpenCodeAdapter processes a session's rows from the real message table (current SQLite generation, ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db-shaped), THE SYSTEM SHALL sum that table's precomputed tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, and tokens_cache_write columns (and the message table's own cost column, stored as TokenEconomics.provided_cost_usd per CRIT-LUMEN-160) into transcript-level TokenEconomics -- these are already-aggregated per-message values maintained by OpenCode itself, not deltas requiring independent computation.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Rewritten against real column names confirmed this session via direct sqlite3 inspection of a live opencode.db (message table carries precomputed cost/tokens_* columns) -- replaces the prior invented accumulated_cost/input_tokens JSONL-line shape, which matched no real OpenCode format. The message/part table's exact column-level layout for turn role and tool-call content (needed for CRIT-LUMEN-112 through 114 below) was not fully characterized this session -- only the token/cost columns were directly verified -- so those criteria are marked as needing one further direct sqlite3 inspection pass before implementation, rather than having their exact column names guessed here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN OpenCodeAdapter processes the current SQLite generation, THE SYSTEM SHALL derive each CanonicalTurn's role and text by joining the message and part tables on session/message id (part holds the message's content payload per real schema; the exact column names for role and text/tool-call discrimination require one further direct sqlite3 inspection of a live opencode.db before this criterion can specify literal field names -- tracked as an open item, not fabricated here).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Honestly incomplete rather than guessed: this session confirmed the real table names (session/message/part/event) and the token/cost column names on message, via direct sqlite3 inspection, but did not inspect part's column layout closely enough to specify exact role/tool-call field names without repeating the same unverified-inference mistake this whole pass exists to correct.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN OpenCodeAdapter processes the LEGACY, pre-1.1, file-based generation (storage/session|message|part/*.json, one JSON object per file rather than SQLite), THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the same message/part join semantics as CRIT-LUMEN-112 adapted to file-based storage, sharing one role/type shape confirmed common to both generations by ccusage's real adapter source -- exact field names carry the same open-item caveat as CRIT-LUMEN-112 pending direct inspection of a real legacy-generation sample file (none was available on this machine, which only has the current SQLite generation installed).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The legacy generation could not be directly verified this session since only a current-generation opencode.db exists on this machine -- flagged honestly as unverified rather than reusing the old, already-disproven action/observation shape.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN OpenCodeAdapter processes a session (either generation), THE SYSTEM SHALL derive tool-call error state from the event table (real table confirmed present in the current SQLite schema) rather than a JSONL "observation" field, which does not exist in any real OpenCode format checked this session.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Replaces the prior invented "observation" field with the real event table now confirmed present -- exact column-level detail for error/is_error carries the same open-item caveat as CRIT-LUMEN-112.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF a row/record in an OpenCode source (SQLite query result or legacy JSON file) is malformed or fails to deserialize into the expected shape, THE SYSTEM SHALL skip it and record a durable, queryable parse-failure entry (per the redesigned CRIT-LUMEN-025) before continuing -- this is CRIT-LUMEN-025's system-wide malformed-record requirement made explicitly testable against OpenCodeAdapter.

THE SYSTEM SHALL provide a synthetic_50mb_session(orchestrator: OrchestratorKind, seed: u64) fixture generator in crates/lumen-fixtures that deterministically expands a real corpus template to at least 50MB without any binary fixture file being checked into the repository, and a criterion benchmark in crates/lumen-session/benches/ SHALL assert that parse_stream over that generated fixture completes in under 35 milliseconds, providing the concrete measurement path CRIT-LUMEN-029 currently lacks. NOTE: this benchmarks parse_stream's actual current reader path (a buffered line reader); it does not itself require memory-mapped I/O, since memmap2 is a declared lumen-session dependency (Cargo.toml) that is not yet used by any parsing code path -- CRIT-LUMEN-029's "memory-mapped" framing is aspirational relative to the current implementation, a pre-existing gap outside this amendment's scope to resolve.

IF a ClaudeCodeAdapter JSONL entry has one of id, cwd, model, sessionId, requestId, version, costUSD, or either cache-token field present but explicitly set to JSON null (not merely absent), THE SYSTEM SHALL treat that entry as malformed per CRIT-LUMEN-025 rather than treating the null as a valid empty/zero value.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: New, real corruption mode confirmed via ccusage's cross-validated Claude adapter (has_unsupported_null_field, lib.rs:868): Claude Code itself sometimes emits these fields as explicit JSON null, not just omits them -- never previously represented in Lumen's model, which would silently misparse null as a default/zero value instead of rejecting the line.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN ClaudeCodeAdapter parses a session's entries, THE SYSTEM SHALL set CanonicalTranscript.otel_conversation_id (a SINGULAR, session-level field -- see the redesigned otel_conversation_id in SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS) from the FIRST non-sidechain entry's requestId encountered in file order that carries one; once set from that entry, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT overwrite it from any later entry's requestId, even when later entries carry a different requestId value (requestId is a real, per-API-call field, not a stable per-conversation value, so a session's entries legitimately carry many different requestId values across turns -- this rule is the explicit reduction from many-per-session to one-per-session). Sidechain entries (isSidechain=true) are skipped entirely when searching for this first value, matching the real tie-break preference confirmed in ccusage's Claude adapter (should_replace_deduped_entry, lib.rs:539: non-sidechain always wins over sidechain).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: requestId is a real, already-present top-level field (confirmed via ccusage's cross-validated adapter), a cleaner native answer than the otel_request_ids side-channel-scanning design it replaces. Audit finding (2026-08-20), confirmed as a real internal contradiction: the prior wording only specified a tie-break for the sidechain-vs-non-sidechain collision case, but requestId is per-API-call, not per-conversation, so a full precedence rule was needed to reduce potentially-many-per-session values down to the one singular otel_conversation_id SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS's field actually requires -- 'first non-sidechain requestId wins, never overwritten' is that rule, now stated explicitly rather than left implicit.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN AgyAdapter locates a session's real transcript, THE SYSTEM SHALL read from ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl directly (or an equivalent already-resolved path) rather than through the ~/.gemini/logs/<id>.jsonl symlink layer, since the symlink is a convenience flattening view, not a guaranteed-present source in every install. THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the sibling ~/.gemini/logs/<id>.json (no "l") summary file -- a structurally different, precomputed Gemini-API role/parts[].text shape -- as out of scope for this adapter (see non_goals).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Provenance fully resolved this session: Google discontinued Gemini CLI for Antigravity CLI (2026-05-19/06-18 transition per Google's own developer blog), and ~/.gemini/logs/*.jsonl was confirmed via direct ls -la on this machine to be a symlink farm into antigravity-cli/brain/, not an independent source.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a session file's first 2048 bytes contain the JSON key "usageMetadata" with nested promptTokenCount/candidatesTokenCount/thoughtsTokenCount/cachedContentTokenCount/totalTokenCount fields, and no ClaudeCode, Antigravity, Codex, or OpenCode fingerprint markers matched first, THE SYSTEM SHALL identify the orchestrator as OrchestratorKind::Qwen via detect_orchestrator, reading real session files from ~/.qwen/projects/<project>/chats/<file>.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: New orchestrator support: ccusage's real Qwen adapter confirms Qwen Code is a real, distinct, actively-used format whose usage fields are named identically to Google's Gemini API response schema (confirming Qwen Code's CLI lineage is Gemini-CLI-derived) -- previously entirely unrepresented; OrchestratorKind (crates/lumen-model/src/transcript.rs:27-34) needs a new Qwen variant added alongside the existing ClaudeCode/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Kimi/GenericOtel set.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23. WHEN any SessionAdapter cannot determine a real model identity for a session (the source data never carries a recognizable model field, or the adapter defaults before any is found), THE SYSTEM SHALL set model_family to an honest, provider-specific placeholder string that PricingTable::is_recognized returns false for ("<provider>-unknown-model", the convention AgyAdapter/CodexAdapter/OpenCodeAdapter/ClaudeCodeAdapter all follow) -- NEVER a real, currently-seeded model name. THE SYSTEM SHALL enforce this as a documented contract on the SessionAdapter trait itself (a doc comment on SessionAdapter in crates/lumen-session/src/adapter.rs establishing it as required behavior for every implementation, including future ones) AND as a machine-checked golden test tying every known adapter's real fallback behavior to one shared expectation, Weaver-style (crates/lumen-session/tests/test_adapter_unknown_model_contract.rs).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-22, HIGH severity, adversarially verified): ClaudeCodeAdapter (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs:37) still defaulted model_family to the literal "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022" -- a real, currently-seeded PricingTable row -- the exact bug class already fixed in CodexAdapter (commit db0c4b1, "gpt-4o" -> "codex-unknown-model") and already avoided in AgyAdapter/OpenCodeAdapter. An assistant turn carrying real usage but no model key silently priced at real Sonnet rates with is_fully_priced=true instead of surfacing as unpriced. FIXED 2026-08-23 (instance bug, commit d337b90; shared contract, this criterion's remaining scope, same day): default changed to "claude-code-unknown-model", following the exact same convention, with a regression test proving both the new default and is_fully_priced=false. Root cause identified by the same audit: the convention was never a formal contract, only inconsistently-restated comments in adapter files with zero mention in SessionAdapter's own trait definition. Research (2026-08-22) into how OpenTelemetry's Weaver enforces instrumentation-library consistency suggested the real fix is a machine-checked contract test per adapter, not just a doc comment -- implemented as both: SessionAdapter's doc comment states the contract explicitly, and test_adapter_unknown_model_contract.rs exercises all 4 known adapters (including OpenCodeAdapter, which implements its own parse_database rather than the SessionAdapter trait, via its own dedicated case following the same shared assertions) against a minimal no-model-field input, asserting the naming convention, PricingTable::is_recognized() == false, and TokenEconomics.is_fully_priced == false uniformly. A 5th adapter added later without extending this test would be missing required coverage, not silently compliant -- the doc comment on SessionAdapter directs a new adapter author to add a case there.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PLANNED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-22). WHEN parsing a JSONL-format session (ClaudeCodeAdapter, CodexAdapter, AgyAdapter), THE SYSTEM SHALL share one implementation of the line-reading/byte-offset-tracking/parse-failure-recording boilerplate across all three adapters, rather than each adapter maintaining its own near-identical copy that must be kept in sync by hand.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-22, low severity but real): claude.rs, codex.rs, and agy.rs all implement byte-offset tracking, the io::Error-as-ParseFailureRecord branch, and the serde_json-error-as-ParseFailureRecord branch nearly verbatim, self-acknowledged in comments (codex.rs/agy.rs both say 'same...rationale as claude.rs'). A shared jsonl_lines() iterator/helper in adapter.rs, consumed by all three, would keep the subtle byte_offset-non-advancement semantics in one place instead of three.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-23. WHEN ClaudeCodeAdapter parses an assistant turn whose tool_calls include a Skill tool_use block, THE SYSTEM SHALL set that turn's CanonicalTurn.attribution to AttributionSource::Skill{name, plugin}, deriving name/plugin from the block's real input.skill field (splitting on ':' -- a plugin-provided skill is named "plugin:skill", e.g. "canon:architect"; a skill with no plugin owner, e.g. "artifact-design", has no colon and plugin is None). Every other turn's attribution SHALL remain None -- THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT guess or propagate attribution to turns downstream of the invocation turn.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Full-codebase semantic-model review finding (2026-08-23): AttributionSource existed as a type with a live consumer (lumen-analysis's AttributionAccumulator) but no adapter ever populated it, so the accumulator always analyzed None. Research against this session's own real ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl logs confirmed the Skill tool_use block's input.skill field is real, structured, and directly recoverable (e.g. {"skill": "artifact-design"}), including colon-namespacing for plugin-provided skills. Also confirmed a real gap: Claude Code does not scope a skill's effect to a sub-transcript the way subagents do (no sibling JSONL, no boundary) -- it injects the skill's instructions into the same ongoing thread -- so there is no structural signal for "this later turn happened because of that earlier skill invocation." User explicitly chose the narrow scope (invocation turn only) over guessing at a cascade heuristic; the cascade-attribution gap is intentionally left undecided rather than silently resolved by an assumption. Regression tests in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_claude.rs: test_claude_code_adapter_attributes_turn_to_plugin_namespaced_skill_invocation, test_claude_code_adapter_attributes_turn_to_unnamespaced_builtin_skill_with_no_plugin, test_claude_code_adapter_non_skill_turns_have_no_attribution, test_claude_code_adapter_turn_with_no_skill_tool_call_has_no_attribution.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-23. WHEN a caller needs to load real sessions from a source without knowing in advance which orchestrator produced it, THE SYSTEM SHALL let every known adapter -- including OpenCodeAdapter -- implement one shared SessionAdapter::load(SessionSource) -> Result<Vec<CanonicalTranscript>, IngestionError> entry point, dispatchable through a single &dyn SessionAdapter reference, where SessionSource is Stream(Box<dyn BufRead>) (one-file-to-one-session JSONL adapters) or Database(&Path) (OpenCodeAdapter's one-file-to-many-sessions SQLite store). An adapter given the source shape it doesn't support SHALL return IngestionError::UnsupportedSourceKind, never silently misinterpret it. Existing parse_stream/parse_database inherent methods on each adapter remain unchanged and are what load delegates to.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Full-codebase architecture review finding (2026-08-23): OpenCodeAdapter could not implement SessionAdapter at all (parse_database(&Path) -> Result<Vec<_>, _> was structurally incompatible with parse_stream(Box<dyn BufRead>) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, _>), forcing lumen-cli's load_sessions to special-case it with a different method name AND a different return shape. User explicitly chose to generalize now (over leaving it as a documented one-off exception) once told the trait was otherwise never used polymorphically anywhere in the workspace, making this a low-risk, low-blast-radius change: parse_stream/parse_database stayed inherent methods (zero existing call sites broke), only a new load method was added per adapter as a thin delegating wrapper. Discovered and fixed in the same pass, as a direct consequence of rewriting lumen-cli's load_sessions to use the new uniform dispatch: ClaudeCodeAdapter::parse_session_with_subagents (CRIT-LUMEN-026, links sibling subagents/*.jsonl files into CanonicalTranscript.subagents) was NEVER called from lumen-cli -- load_sessions called bare parse_stream directly -- so CRIT-LUMEN-176's rolled_up_economics and CRIT-LUMEN-179's per-subagent anomaly detection were both correctly implemented but inert for every real `lumen ingest`/`lumen audit` run, since subagents was always empty in practice. load_sessions now special-cases ClaudeCode specifically (not through the generic load(source) path) to call parse_session_with_subagents instead, since sibling-file discovery inherently needs a real filesystem directory that SessionSource deliberately abstracts away -- documented inline as the one adapter-specific exception this design still has, and why. Regression test: crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs's load_session_links_sibling_subagent_files_and_rolls_up_their_cost, plus crates/lumen-session/tests/test_session_source.rs's dispatch-uniformity and wrong-source-kind tests.
